Team preview. Bringing Incineroar (lead: Intimidate and Fake Out for support), Garchomp (Earthquake hits Tyranitar, Metagross, Incineroar), and Gholdengo (special coverage against Dragonite, Weavile, Metagross). Watch for Rotom-Wash's Levitate blanking Earthquake, and Weavile's speed and Ice moves. Keep Garchomp away from Weavile's Ice Punch.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I need to pick 3 Pokémon against their team of Tyranitar, Metagross, Dragonite, Rotom-Wash, Weavile, and Incineroar, weighing their various weaknesses. Garchomp stands out since its dragon typing and ground/fire coverage hits several of these hard.

I'll go with Incineroar for the lead with intimidate and fake out support, pair it with Gholdengo for coverage against Dragonite, Incineroar, and Weavile, and round it out with Garchomp.

decisions.thought: 48% MOVE: earthquake, 30% MOVE: stealthrock, 10% MOVE: stoneedge

Lead matchup: my Incineroar (Intimidate, already dropped Tyranitar's Attack) vs their Tyranitar, which set Sandstorm. Fake Out only works on my first turn, so I'm using it now to flinch and stop Tyranitar acting. Next: Garchomp with Earthquake or Stone Edge can hit Tyranitar hard. Watch for Rotom-Wash's Levitate blanking Earthquake, and Weavile's speed and Ice Punch, which threatens Garchomp. Gholdengo covers Dragonite and Weavile.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Checking the first turn with Incineroar's Fake Out against Tyranitar — since Tyranitar is Rock/Dark, I need to verify the type effectiveness since Rock typically resists Normal-type moves, which would explain why it's flagged as not very effective.

I'll use Fake Out anyway since the flinch is what matters here, not the chip damage — it's a one-time tool only available this turn, so it's worth using now against Tyranitar regardless of the reduced damage.

decisions.thought: 55% MOVE: earthquake, 22% MOVE: stealthrock, 11% MOVE: stoneedge

Turn 2: Incineroar's Dark and Fire attacks are resisted by Tyranitar (Rock/Dark), so I'm pivoting out with Parting Shot. That drops Tyranitar's Attack and Sp. Atk again and brings in Garchomp, which outspeeds it (169 vs 72-124). Garchomp's Earthquake is 2x on Tyranitar. Watch for Rotom-Wash's Levitate blanking Earthquake, and Weavile's Ice Punch threatening Garchomp. Gholdengo covers Dragonite and Weavile later. Tyranitar's Leftovers and Sandstorm are still active.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Incineroar is at 190/202 against Tyranitar at 99% with Atk lowered. Since Tyranitar is Rock/Dark, its own Dark typing resists Darkest Lariat, so I should lean on Flare Blitz instead since Fire isn't ideal but still better than a resisted move.

Switching to Garchomp looks strong since Earthquake hits Tyranitar super effectively while Garchomp takes little from Rock or Dark moves and outspeeds it at 169 Speed. Using Parting Shot with Incineroar could be even better, dropping Tyranitar's Attack further while bringing Garchomp in safely for free.

decisions.thought: Plan: Garchomp (Mega-capable, Garchompite) comes in to hit Tyranitar with Earthquake (2x). Watch Rotom-Wash Levitate blanking Earthquake, and Weavile's Ice Punch threatening Garchomp. Gholdengo covers Dragonite and Weavile. 36% MOVE: stealthrock, 17% MOVE: earthquake, 15% SWITCH: metagross

Turn 3: Garchomp is faster than all their Pokémon except possibly Weavile (130-194 Spe), so it moves first against Tyranitar. Tyranitar is at -2 Atk from Intimidate and Parting Shot. I'm Mega-evolving Garchomp now for Sand Force plus Earthquake. Opponent known: Tyranitar (Leftovers, Earthquake, Sandstorm). Remaining threats: Rotom-Wash (Levitate blanks Earthquake), Weavile (Ice Punch vs Garchomp), Dragonite, Metagross. Gholdengo covers Dragonite, Weavile and Metagross. Keep Incineroar for Fake Out or Parting Shot later.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Tyranitar's Attack is down two stages from parting shot and intimidate, and it's Rock/Dark so Garchomp's Earthquake hits for double damage. I'm also factoring in that Mega Garchomp's Sand Force ability would boost Ground-type moves further in the sandstorm.

Earthquake is neutral against Garchomp itself, so Tyranitar's retaliation isn't a major threat. Garchomp outspeeds Tyranitar anyway, so I'll go ahead and Mega Evolve now and fire off Earthquake.

decisions.thought: 35% MOVE: extremespeed, 35% MOVE: outrage, 13% MOVE: earthquake

Tyranitar is down. Garchomp (Mega, faster than Dragonite) is now facing Dragonite. Earthquake does nothing to Flying types, so I'm using Dragon Claw (STAB, 100% accuracy, super effective) instead. Dragonite may have Multiscale, which halves damage at full HP, so the first hit may not KO. Watch for Rotom-Wash (Levitate blanks Earthquake), Weavile (Ice Punch threatens Garchomp), and Metagross. Gholdengo covers Metagross and Weavile. Incineroar (134 HP) can use Parting Shot or Fake Out later.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Dragonite is still at full health while Garchomp, who's faster, can't touch it with Earthquake since Flying types are immune to Ground. But Garchomp's Stone Edge and Dragon Claw both hit Dragonite for super effective damage, so I'm weighing how dangerous that matchup really is.

Comparing options: Dragon Claw gets STAB and 100% accuracy, outdamaging Stone Edge once the accuracy and effective power are factored in, so Dragon Claw is the better move here regardless of Dragonite's ability.

decisions.thought: Opponent: Tyranitar fainted (Earthquake). Dragonite at 39% is the active threat, it revealed Extreme Speed and may have Multiscale. Garchomp Mega outspeeds it. decisions.hidden_reasoning: Dragonite is at 39% health after sandstorm chip, but Garchomp outspeeds and both Stone Edge and Dragon Claw hit it super effectively, so Dragonite's roughly 70 HP won't survive another hit of that magnitude.

Gholdengo can handle Weavile and Metagross later. Incineroar at 134 HP can Parting Shot.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Metagross is already at 75% and Garchomp outspeeds it with Earthquake being super effective against Steel-types, so that's clearly the best move regardless of what ability or moveset Metagross is running.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Dragonite's at 39% while Mega Garchomp is at 137/185 and outspeeds it. Checking type matchups: Dragon Claw hits neutrally since Flying doesn't resist Dragon, and Stone Edge would be super effective against the Flying typing.

Since Dragonite isn't at full HP, Multiscale isn't active, so Garchomp's Dragon Claw with its boosted Attack and STAB should be enough for the KO. I'll go with Dragon Claw for the reliable accuracy.
